label: first copy-phase input is "3" (echo of original token 0 = 3)
explanation: Fires at the step right after <DEL> + 1 (recall_idx 1), when the input is the fed-back first original token and that token is the digit 3, i.e. sequences starting with 3. In this case it fires on essentially every such sequence at strong magnitude (0.45-1.0 of max), with no false positives on dev. It does not fire in the original phase, at the delimiter, or at later copy steps. Weak residual activations (about 1% of mass, under ~0.1 of max) occur at the same step when the first token is something else, mostly m, e, t, g, or j. Magnitude is highest for short sequences (L=4-6) and when the next tokens are letters like m/w; it is lower for long sequences.

issues: Minor caveat about the explanation: active-step counts and mass are split roughly evenly by length. On test, L<=6 gives recall 0.39 and mass 0.52, and L>=7 gives recall 0.39 and mass 0.47. Short sequences have a somewhat higher firing rate per step, but long sequences fire at full strength too. This matches the explanation's own hedge ('did not check systematically'), and the label makes no claim about length.

The misses on test are 4737 steps holding 1.4% of the mass. All are faint (<=0.07 of max) and fall at recall_idx 1 or 2. The input tokens vary (e, m, g, r, and also 3 at recall_idx 2). This is low-magnitude noise with no strong systematic class. The recall of 0.777 is explained by these faint activations alone: coverage by activation quartile is 0.11 for the bottom quartile and 1.0 for the other three.

Precision is 0.99994 on test, with a single false positive ('3 3 3 <DEL> 3'). The claimed profile checks out on dev: zero activity at the delimiter, original-phase mass 0.001, recall_idx 2 mass 0.003, and nothing at recall_idx 3 or later.
